thread.title: Dubas discusses Penguins' youth development and prospects after playoff exit
thread.title_full: Dubas discusses Penguins' youth development and prospects after playoff exit

author: Keystone Today
title: Dubas discusses Penguins' youth development and prospects after playoff exit
text:
The Pittsburgh Penguins’ President of Hockey Operations and General Manager Kyle Dubas said on May 13 that the organization is closely monitoring the progress of its young players, as both minor league affiliates continue their postseason runs. The remarks come two weeks after the Penguins were eliminated by the Philadelphia Flyers in the first round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs.
Dubas said that every playoff round won by Wilkes-Barre/Scranton (AHL) and Wheeling Nailers (ECHL) offers further opportunities for player development. “Every round they win is an opportunity to continue to develop and make our decisions harder for next fall, where they’re going to have to earn it,” Dubas said. “But that will guide a lot of our decision-making here. So, we’ll watch that closely.”
Goaltending was a major topic, with Dubas praising performances at all levels. He highlighted Arturs Silovs’ strong play late in the NHL playoffs: “I thought our goaltending was very, very good at some stretches and struggled at others, and it stabilized itself at the end with Arty having a great performance in the back half of the series against Philly.” Dubas also noted upcoming decisions regarding free agents Stuart Skinner and Silovs while expressing confidence in prospects Sergei Murashov and Joel Blomqvist: “My full expectation is that two of them, Sergei and Joel, will be competing for a roster spot here this year.” Taylor Gauthier’s progression was also recognized: “We have a lot of confidence in Taylor and think he’s earned that as well… it’s an area of good strength and depth for us. But the guys have earned that.”
Among skaters, Bill Zonnon’s commitment drew praise from Dubas: “He had been watching every game and studying the systems… He’s deeply committed to doing all the small things.” Zonnon scored his first AHL goal shortly after joining Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. Quoted by Tony Androckitis following his debut game, Zonnon said: “Honestly, I don’t remember the last time I had this much fun playing… just having fun, believing in myself, and I knew good things were going to happen.” Rutger McGroarty’s development was discussed as he overcame injury setbacks; Dubas called him “an excellent penalty killer” who has improved his skating.
Ville Koivunen’s journey included early struggles but ended with improvement: “He went down to the minors… we felt objectively his speed improved… he had improved,” Dubas said. Harrison Brunicke’s adjustment as a young defenseman received attention: “It’s hard,” Dubas said about Brunicke’s start as a 19-year-old NHL player but added he is now making an impact during AHL playoffs.
Owen Pickering was another focus among defensemen; according to Dubas: “We’ve been very happy with the way Owen has come on here in the second half of the year.”
The Pittsburgh Penguins are recognized for their notable figures including Hall of Fame players, coaches, executives; consistent playoff appearances; community ties; hosting games at PPG Paints Arena; ownership by Fenway Sports Group; all according to their official website .
Looking ahead, Dubas emphasized competition among prospects for roster spots next season while underscoring continued organizational focus on developing young talent.

Dubas said that every playoff round won by Wilkes-Barre/Scranton (AHL) and Wheeling Nailers (ECHL) offers further opportunities for player development.
